newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gilts recover, banks await fresh funds flow.
newsitem.headline: Indian gilts recover, banks await fresh funds flow.

text.p: Gilt prices recovered after an initial fall on Tuesday while call money remained steady, dealers said.
"There was some unexpected selling pressure in the morning," a dealer at a state-run bank said.
"Prices of government securities fell initially but picked up later in the afternoon as buyers returned to the market."
He said the market appeared to be overheated and was due for a correction. Buying interest in securities continued at a high level as banks are sitting on a pile of money, he said.
"With credit disbursals not picking up, banks are looking to park their funds somewhere or the other," he said.
Dealers said prices of government securities would continue to rise, given the abundant liquidity in the banking system.
Liquidity will receive a further boost on Saturday when a half-percentage point cut in banks' cash reserve ratio comes into effect. This is expected to release around 21 billion rupees to banks.
Call money ended Tuesday in the 3.75-4.0 percent range, little changed from 3.50-4.0 percent opening, dealers said.
In the secondary market, the 13.50 percent 1997 was traded on Tuesday at a yield of 10.10 percent against Monday's 10.12 percent, dealers said.
There were no trades in certificates of deposit or commercial papers, they said. Certificates of deposit were quoted around 11.0 percent, the dealer said.
"Currently, commercial paper from top-rated companies is being quoted between 12.0 and 12.50 percent," a dealer said. "But we are getting only quotes and no deals are being struck."
